When I was like 12 or so, I went to camp, where some guys had a CD of Johnny Rebel...

This was in the Deep South of the United States circa. 1999, btw.

Disclaimer

Let me just tell you, that I have no info on Johnny Rebel. This is simply a summary of what I witnessed while these guys were playing this CD in the cabin. In no way do I agree with the songs, nor even think they hold a place in 21st century society. (In fact I was rather horrified that I was witness to 1850's Klan mentality...)

There were songs about black people being useless and harmful to society. I'm pretty sure lynching was mentioned. I also think that there was emphasis on knowing your place in society, thereby frowning upon social advancement.

There was a song about a black man who worked as a bagger in a grocery store who scared the customers away because of body odor.

There was a song about a white woman and a black man who elloped. Apparently this signalled the "End Times" because I'm stil waiting for a valid reason.

None of these songs, I support in any way. But I'm pretty sure you could still call that taboo even by today's standards.

I have to agree with you, wireless is only good for phones and tablets, sometimes laptops for light internet use. I go by the philosophy that if you want reliability you should always go wired. In my current place before I moved in I asked the landlord if I could run a cat 5 from the basement where the cable modem is to the living room. I also have a trendnet Ethernet over Powerlines device that runs from there to my top floor and a wifi router in AP mode connected to it. Mind you I only get 6Mb/s but that's good enough for light devices like phones and tablets. My gaming rig is wired, my netflix device is also wired.

You could try an Ethernet over Powerline adapter, however you need to know that if they are not on the same circuit the advertised speed will drop.
